headline.process: Rain-associated acoustic expansion is recurrent activation of a latent species-by-site chorus network, not simple amplification of an already-active chorus.
headline.proximal_environment: Among tested weather/hydric covariates, wet-minus-dry shallow soil-water change is the strongest and most transportable environmental correlate of strong CI2-3 and CI3 recruitment and of third-plus spatial depth.
headline.local_template: Strictly prior species x physical-SiteID chorus history predicts where reactivation occurs, beyond generic site quality and sampling effort.
headline.architecture: The safest model has partially distinct temporal/environmental and spatial-template axes: rain recency remains informative, soil-water change adds strong hydric-state information, and local species x site history supplies spatial memory. A simple soil-wetting-sign gate and a simple soil x local-memory interaction are not supported.
headline.spatial_consequence: Once a route-new species activates, the unusual matrix signal lies mainly in third-and-later-stop participation. Conditional on species identity and realized wet-side stop count, special stop placement is unnecessary.
headline.generality: Soil-water and local-template effects are robust across NAAMP route/time splits and leave-one-state-out tests, but state-specific slopes are heterogeneous and cross-continental universality remains unestablished.

soil_protocol_window.interpretation: Soil association is not confined to comparisons wholly inside the 0-3-day protocol window; the much smaller both-outside subset is directionally positive but imprecise.

same_observer_soil_plus_template_depth.interpretation: Coupling appears in the smaller robust subset, but the full-sample interaction is not supported; do not make multiplicative gating the headline.

alternatives_not_sufficient: simple attraction to already-active chorus stops
NWI hydroperiod as the strong-chorus mediator
Palustrine versus Riverine/Lacustrine NWI class as the strong-chorus mediator
current light rain at the survey
72-hour precipitation amount after soil-water change is included
a simple binary gate requiring wet-side soil water to exceed dry-side soil water
generic good-frog-site quality instead of species-specific local memory
local memory alone as a generator of the matrix geometry
species-specific rainfall shifts alone as a generator of the full matrix geometry
special stop placement after species identity and realized occupied-stop count are fixed

safest_current_model.name: partially_distinct_hydric_state_plus_local_template_model
safest_current_model.statement: Rain-recency-defined wet surveys contain more strong acoustic recruitment, while wet-minus-dry soil-water change provides additional, broadly transportable hydric-state information and strictly prior species x SiteID chorus history provides spatial memory. The two latter axes independently predict post-activation spatial depth in the full sample.
safest_current_model.temporal_environmental_axis: Recent rain and environmental wetting are related but not interchangeable. Soil-water change is a stronger predictor than 72-hour rain amount and generalizes strongly, yet rain-recency effects do not disappear specifically when soil wetting has the opposite sign; simple mediation/gating is therefore unsupported.
safest_current_model.spatial_axis: Historical own-species use of the same physical SiteID predicts future strong chorus beyond generic site productivity, and the effect decays with distance.
safest_current_model.matrix_axis: Historical template breadth and soil-water change both predict third-and-later-stop depth. Once species identity and realized depth k are fixed, special placement geometry is not required.
safest_current_model.unresolved: The acoustic data cannot separate persistent local populations from persistent species-specific microhabitat suitability, and ERA5 soil water cannot distinguish frog hydration from breeding-site/inundation processes.

generality.within_NAAMP: Strong. Soil-water and local-template effects reproduce across route/time splits and leave-one-state-out analyses, although state-specific effects remain heterogeneous.
generality.across_taxa: Strongly suggestive within NAAMP; site-template signs are positive in 19/20 estimable species and strong-activation contributions are diffuse.
generality.cross_continent: Not established. Available external public data do not provide an effort-complete comparable species x site matrix, and AnuraSet site tests did not reproduce the prefixed threshold-dominance rule.

do_not_claim: Soil moisture is a proven causal mediator of rainfall.
Positive soil wetting is necessary for the rain-recency effect.
A fixed biological soil-moisture threshold has been identified.
ERA5 soil water is frog body hydration or pond depth.
Rain causes demographic colonization, abundance increase or reproductive success.
The same individuals return to the same sites.
The mechanism is universal across continents.
stop_rule: Further NAAMP post-readback modeling should stop unless it tests a qualitatively new alternative unavailable in the current hierarchy. Highest-value next evidence is direct survey-night hydrology/body hydration or an independent effort-complete multi-site acoustic time series.
